newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares ease, seen staying flat this week.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares ease, seen staying flat this week.

text.p: Polish shares eased after a three-session rise and analysts said the market would likely stay in a flat trend after the jump at the turn of the month that followed steeper falls in late October.

"The market has been weak lately and that's how it looks for the short term -- (firms') October earnings results were good but not good enough to return us to a growth trend," said Jan Koch, a trader at Polish Development Bank (PBR) house.
The market surged this year about 100 percent by early October. Analysts said the stronger sellling after price-fixing signalled a fall was more likely for Thursday.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.6 percent to 13,595.8 points and turnover fell 13.8 percent to 72.7 million zlotys on both markets.

Analysts said the lower house of parliament's possible vote on Thursday on the Senate's amendments to 1997's tax bill could provide the next signal. Last week the Senate removed the lower house's steep tax cuts for low earners, seen as inflationary.
"The market should react positively to any prudent decision," said Pawel Hominski, an analyst at Magnus brokerage.
Some analysts said the Senate's tax rates were already priced in by the market after the the Senate's vote last week.
Analysts said the scale of biggest loser Mostostal Export's five-percent loss in low turnover was accidental. The stock showed stronger buying after price-fixing.
Continuous trade turnover was 0.8 million zlotys with four stocks up and two down.
NFI units rose 1.4 percent to 150 zlotys and rose 3.8 percent to 152 zlotys in 19.3-million-zloty live trade.
Analysts said the units were rising this week despite some fears of selling before Friday's deadline for Poles to buy the unit on the primary market for 20 zlotys.
